events.excerpt: Nixie clocks have become popular enough that these days there’s no shortage of turn-key options that let you experience that warm glow with a minimum of fuss. Many still come as little more than a bare PCB, giving the purchaser some freedom to come up with their own enclosure, but at least the electronics are handled. But for [Justin Scott], putting his new two-digit Nixie clock board into a handsome box was only half the battle . He also wanted to do something a bit more interesting than just tell the time. To convert the board from a simple clock to a device that could show how many minutes until the next bus showed up at his local stop, he had to hack the firmware and establish a communication link to a Raspberry Pi to do the heavy lifting. The first step was to get a modified firmware on the clock PCB, and that required a ST-LINK V2 programmer and some time tracing out the pins on the STM8 microcontroller to determine how they controlled the various elements of the Nixie tubes. Fortunately, there were just I/O pins left over to stand up a serial link to a Raspberry Pi Zero through a level converter. events.excerpt: TL;DR: Chainlink and Moody's Ratings completed a cross-chain distribution pilot using test data. It ran on testnets and did not publish live rating actions or change Moody's existing publication processes. Tokenized finance needs information to move alongside assets. In a November 10 announcement , Chainlink and Moody's Ratings reported a completed pilot that used the Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol, or CCIP, to distribute credit information across multiple networks. The exercise connected Moody's Token Integration Engine, known as TIE, with cross-chain messaging. Its significance lies in a familiar market problem: investors need consistent information about an instrument even when different pieces of financial infrastructure represent or hold it. A ratings-distribution test with defined limits The pilot used representative data in a controlled testnet environment, spanning permissioned and permissionless networks. No actual rating actions were published onchain, and live dissemination processes were not involved. That scope makes the result useful as an interoperability test. It leaves the separate work of operating a production service, setting responsibilities and integrating it with financial institutions. Consider a hypothetical bond represented across several networks
events.headline: Chainlink and Moody’s Complete Testnet Pilot for Cross-Chain Credit Ratings

events.excerpt: The next version of the C++ programming language may be delayed at the last minute due to a dispute over a security-enhancing Contracts feature. Contracts have deeply split C++ technical maintainers. One group backs the C++ creator Bjarne Stroustrup , who is against the technology in its present form in grounds it was hastily implemented. But others are eager to see Contracts implemented, even arguing the tech's detractors are poisoning the C++ development process itself. The disagreement boiled over just before a vote to ratify the new version of the language. In October, the Draft International Standard (DIS) of C++26 failed its ISO ballot — the next-to-last stage in the International Organization for Standardization’s approval process during which a standard's technical details are formally ratified by a set of national standards bodies. The ballot saw 13 votes cast in favor, 9 against, and 12 abstentions, failing to meet the ISO requirement of having no more than 25 percent negative votes. Contracts was the major sticking point for those voting nay. Helius's launch announcement introduces Privacy Rings as programmable pools that execute on Solana, giving developers tools for private payments and financial applications on the same network. The feature addresses a practical obstacle for public-ledger payments. A business may want the settlement benefits of a blockchain without publishing every payment amount to competitors or employees. Individual users can have similar concerns about exposing the size and history of their financial activity. Confidentiality has a specific boundary The technical documentation separates confidentiality from anonymity. events.excerpt: Working in tech support can be thankless when gormless colleagues leave you sleepless. Which is why, each Friday, The Register runs a new instalment of On Call – the reader contributed column which ensures your work to keep tech alive doesn't remain unnoticed. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Tim" who told us that while working for a phone company he once rewrote 2,650 lines of C as a six line shell script. He performed that feat after being asked to fix a data transfer program that, strangely, included a bespoke implementation of the venerable File Transfer Protocol (FTP). "Writing the script took eight hours, most of it tracking down the source code of FTP so I could see if it would do what I wanted," Tim wrote. This story took place before the World Wide Web became the way to find information online. To find the code he needed, Tim therefore used a Wide Area Information Server (WAIS) to search remote databases. "In those days, there was no Linux and AT&T had licensed the Unix source code to universities with the strict proviso that it never be made publicly available," Tim explained. events.excerpt: TL;DR: TokenLogic proposes changes to Aave's reserve factors across 54 reserves. Its model estimates $3.5 million in additional annual revenue, using November 9 balances and rates; governance has not yet approved the changes. Aave's latest revenue proposal focuses on how lending income is divided. A November 12 submission from TokenLogic covers 12 V3 instances and V2 Ethereum, with the modeled blended reserve factor rising from 12.0% to 12.7%. The practical issue is straightforward: the protocol treasury would retain a larger share of interest, leaving a smaller share for suppliers where a change applies. Whether that improves the economics over time depends partly on how those suppliers respond. What the reserve factor controls Aave's official FAQ defines the reserve factor as the percentage of borrowing interest that accrues to the treasury. It is set for each asset through governance. The treasury is controlled by Aave Governance, rather than functioning as a conventional company's bank account. A simplified example makes the mechanism clearer. Suppose borrowers generate $100 of interest and a reserve factor is 20%. Before considering other mechanics, $20 goes to the treasury and $80 remains for suppliers. The operation involved law enforcement agencies in 14 countries to pursue drug sellers and buyers on the dark web. Investigators did not say how much of the $234 million represented drug-sale proceeds. The remaining question now is: Will removing drug vendors and seizing assets reduce future sales, or will the business simply move to another marketplace? A record JCODE takedown across four continents The operation known as Operation TorNado was aimed at individuals believed to be engaged in the trade of drugs via dark web marketplaces. This was the sixth and, to date, greatest international effort by the U.S. Justice Department’s Joint Criminal Opioid and Darknet Enforcement (JCODE) team since 2018. The operation was based on Operation RapTor in 2025, which was founded on the evidence gathered from the four previously dismantled markets, namely: Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom, and Tor2Door. events.excerpt: Bitcoin has dipped below $69,000, reaching its lowest level in three months. At the time of writing Bitcoin has witnessed a sharp selloff of more than 7% over the past two days. The broader crypto market has also seen a notable downturn with the total crypto market cap now falling by over 9% this past week. Coinglass data shows that 24 hour long liquidations across crypto have reached $1.31 billion. Bitcoin is Trading Well Below its Bull Market Support Band Bitcoin’s bull market support band is a useful weekly chart indicator which shows two lines, the 20-week simple moving average and the 21-week exponential moving average. Traders and technical analysts keep a close eye on the gap between them. In bullish uptrends, Bitcoin tends to hold above the band or use it as support during a pullback. When prices break below this band, the momentum or trend has usually lost its footing. BTC tested the band as support in early November. It has since fallen well below this range after an accelerated selloff. The support band now sits between $73,570 and $76,530 and traders will now be closely watching this area as overhead resistance if BTC were to stage a recovery rally.
